w: After darshan of Thakorji, Pramukh Swami Maharaj came to the circumambulation path. Tapodhan Bhagat, who looks after the cowshed here, was standing in the circumambulation path. Swamishri asked him, "Did you go to Hira's last rites yesterday or not?" (This was about Hirabhai Bharwad, a devotee who had served in the cowshed since the time of Shastriji Maharaj and had passed away.)
Tapodhan Bhagat said, "I went."

Swamishri said, "We are to do all the rites that follow. The ashes must have been collected. Take them and go to Gadhada. Immerse the ashes there. Take his sons too. Whatever expense there is, we are to bear it all."
Even the humblest servant who serves Thakorji and the organisation with devotion becomes like family to Swamishri. This shows his equal vision.

On a later day, about thirty Bharwads, including Ragho Bharwad, came for Swamishri's darshan. Swamishri met them in the assembly hall. On the thirteenth day after the passing of Hira Bharwad, who had lived in the mandir all his life and served in the cowshed, Swamishri had fed their community on behalf of the mandir. The organisation had borne the cost of cooking 14 maunds of laddus and of the funeral feast. Swamishri's practical graciousness made an impression on the whole community. Ragho Bharwad said to Swamishri, "It is you who have truly served Hira. In our community there is praise everywhere that Swamishri has done everything for Hira, right up to the final feast."
Swamishri said, "Hira was our own man."

The Bharwads enjoyed this affection of Swamishri. In Swamishri's love for a seemingly ordinary devotee like Hira Bharwad, the great mantra "atmavat sarvabhuteshu" (seeing oneself in all beings) echoed.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj had darshan of Thakorji and came to the circumambulation path. Tapodhan Bhagat, who looks after the gaushala (cowshed) here, was standing on the path. Swamishri asked him, "Did you go to Hira's last rites yesterday or not?" Swamishri installed the canvas murtis of Akshar Purushottam, Radha Krishna and Guru parampara (formerly at the old A.P. Mandir in Nairobi) with Vedic rites at the mandir in Nakuru.
In the morning, Swamishri visited the holy places sanctified by Shriji Maharaj in Mandvi. The murti of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj (Thakorji) was honored by the devotees during the morning assembly.
At 5.45 p.m., Swamishri visited the Swaminarayan Gurukul in Koday and blessed the students.
Then Swamishri visited the 72 Jinalay in the village of Talvana.
Thereafter, Swamishri arrived at the village of Khakhar and addressed a small assembly.
At 7.45 p.m., Swamishri arrived back in Bhuj and addressed the evening satsang assembly.
In the morning, Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha ceremony for the new marble murtis of the guru parampara in the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Mombasa.

Today, the murti of Neelkanth Varni was to be installed in the Abhishek Mandapam in Akshardham. All the arrangements to carry the murti in a palanquin from the shikharbaddh mandir to Akshardham were made. Alongwith the senior sadhus Swamishri also shouldered the palanquin from the mandir sanctum to its steps. Thereafter the senior sadhus shouldered the palanquin and the murti was taken in a procession led by sadhus and devotees singing the Swaminarayan dhun.

At 10.00 am Swamishri arrived at the Abhishek Mandapam and performed the rituals in installing the murti of Neelkanth Varni. Thereafter Swamishri bathed the murti with panchamrut and prayed that Neelkanth Varni fulfills the wishes of everyone. Tadagotsarg Ritual : After the ritual installation of the murti of Neelkanth Varni Swamishri engaged himself in the sanctification rituals of the water of Narayan Sarovar. In conclusion Swamishri blessed the occasion, “We believe that water is a god – Jaldev. Now Narayan Sarovar has been sanctified by all devas. We have done pujan of all the devas. There are four main holy lakes in India, namely, Man Sarovar, Pushkar Sarovar near Ajmer, Pampa Sarovar in the south and Narayan Sarovar in the west in Kutch. Maharaj has visited all these places and sanctified them. Here, the water of all pilgrim places and rivers have been poured. If anyone wishes to go on a pilgrimage then by coming here one gets the darshan of God, darshan of Akshardham and all the murtis of the devas. Whoever does darshan, sprinkles water on his head and bathes in its water will be liberated.” At 7.00 pm a special assembly for 6,600 male volunteers and 1400 female volunteers was held in the marquee at Pramukh Swami Nagar. Swamishri blessed the volunteers with words of inspiration and glory for the services they had been blessed with.

st.t: A Spiritual Travelogue of Pramukh Swami Maharaj - New Delhi Page-6, 11 October 2005
w: Tadakutsarg Rituals Swamishri and sadhus ritually pour the waters of 151 rivers and lakes sanctified by Bhagwan Swaminarayan into Narayan Sarovar and bestow it with sacredness. Thereafter Swamishri performed mantra pushpanjali and arti of Narayan Sarovar.
Today, while Mahant Swami Maharaj was writing letters, seeing the heap of letters piled before him, the sadhus asked Swamishri, "Don't you get bored signing so many letters?"
"No. I don't get bored at all," Swamishri said naturally.
Proving this answer of his, today he enjoyed the privilege of devotion by signing 256 letters without a break.

After his puja was over, Mahant Swami Maharaj went to his room to take his medicine. Meanwhile, as part of the Samp Din (Day of Unity) programme, before Swamishri's blessings, Swamishri was to touch the heads of four devotees standing on the stage, one by one, with his staff.
The attendant sadhu explained this to Swamishri and asked, "Will you touch them with the staff or place your hand?"
Swamishri, ever absorbed in the glory of the guru, said, "The staff befits Bapa (Pramukh Swami Maharaj). So I will place my hand."
Adarshswarupdas Swami said, "You are one and the same!"
Not giving up his das bhav (attitude of being a servant), Swamishri said, "Yes, but I will place my hand."
Swamishri came onto the stage and, as understood earlier, placed his hand on the heads of all four devotees.
Today, during the meetings, Yogeshbhai Patel said to Mahant Swami Maharaj, "You once stayed at my home. The house next to Maftabhai Dada's."
Swamishri said, "Yes, he lives right on the main road."

Swamishri had stayed at Yogeshbhai's home for just one night, around 1996 or 1997! Even so, Swamishri remembered that the house next to Maftabhai Dada's is on the main road! This is not possible without closeness with the devotees.

Mahant Swami Maharaj sat on his bed to rest. Then sitopaladi (an Ayurvedic powder) mixed with honey was given to Swamishri in a spoon. Swamishri did not leave even a single grain in the spoon and, as every day, licked it completely clean.
The attendant sadhu said, "You did not leave even a little in the spoon!"
Swamishri, who insists on precision and thrift, said calmly, "Why should I leave any?"
This has been his way from the beginning, for years. Giving a golden lesson through his conduct, Swamishri went to rest.
At 10:00 at night, Mahant Swami Maharaj sat on his bed to retire. Swamishri shone a torch on all the sadhus. His attendant asked, "With what thought did you shine the torch on all the sadhus?"
One of the sadhus said, "A gaze of divinity, so that they become brahmarup."

Swamishri said, "Everyone interprets it differently." Then he said, "For us, there is a constant thought: may everyone become brahmarup (one with the qualities of Brahman). When I do pradakshina (circumambulation) of Nilkanth Varni every day, I keep the thought that everyone may become brahmarup."
We see Swamishri doing pradakshina, but only today did we learn that even while doing pradakshina he is thinking of us.
